title: Yara and the Sigil
premise: Kestrel Delacroix survives in the warded city of Vell by stealing memories and selling them as charms, hiding the sigil burned into his palm since childhood—a mark that once belonged to Yara, the memory-witch who saved his life and vanished. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark, Kestrel learns the sigil is the last living key to the Understar, an ancient power both the mage-hunting Inquisition and the exiled Thorn Court will kill to claim. Hunted through a city unraveling without its wards, Kestrel is forced into an uneasy alliance with Yara's estranged daughter, Sable, who blames him for her mother's disappearance. In the end, Kestrel must choose between erasing the sigil—and every memory of Yara—to save himself, or feeding it his own remembered past to relight the stars, knowing the price of survival was never meant to be paid alone.
about_author: Felix Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed, an experience that left him obsessed with what people choose to remember. He writes fantasy from a small apartment above a shuttered pawnshop, where he insists the previous owner still lends him ideas.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Hours
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A night of routine thefts: he lifts a widow's grief and a merchant's first love, selling them as charms in Vell's gray market while dodging Inquisition wardens. The chapter establishes his rules—never steal a whole life, never be remembered. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking deep fear of being seen.

chapters.title: What the Palm Remembers
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. After a job, the sigil on his palm burns for the first time in five years, showing him a flash of Yara's face. He visits his fence, Odile, who warns him someone has been asking about 'the marked thief.' Emotional beat: dread rekindled; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The border wards fall with a sound like breaking glass; the sky goes black starless. Panic floods Vell, wardens lock the gates, and Kestrel realizes the sigil flared at the exact moment of collapse. Emotional beat: the safe world ending; invisibility now impossible.

chapters.title: A Girl Who Hates My Name
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Introduced ambushing Kestrel in an alley, blade to his throat, convinced he betrayed her mother Yara. She carries half of a broken compass that points toward him instead of north. Emotional beat: fury and grief entangled; reluctant truce forced by a warden patrol.

chapters.title: The Inquisition's Kind Offer
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Warden-Captain Brannoc offers Kestrel immunity if he helps identify surviving magic-users—while making clear the alternative is a pyre. Kestrel pretends to consider, learning the Inquisition already knows about the sigil. Emotional beat: cornered cleverness; the hunter offering a leash.

chapters.title: Memories I Never Lived
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She shows Kestrel Yara's journal, written in a cipher only readable through stolen memories. When Kestrel touches it, he experiences fragments of Yara's life he never stole—including her final night, fleeing something called the Thorn Court. Emotional beat: intimacy with the dead; guilt sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Market of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He returns to the gray market to buy passage out and finds it burning—wardens purging charm-sellers. He saves Odile but must use the sigil openly to do it, witnessed by dozens. Emotional beat: sacrifice of anonymity; first open act of magic.

chapters.title: Thorns in the Dark
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Agents of the exiled Thorn Court capture them, led by the courteous, terrifying Lord Ashvine, who claims Yara stole the sigil's secret from them. He offers Sable her mother's location in exchange for Kestrel. Emotional beat: seductive villainy; loyalty tested by hope.

chapters.title: Five Years of Lies
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Escaping Ashvine, Kestrel confesses to Sable the truth: Yara didn't vanish—she gave Kestrel the sigil willingly and erased his memory of why, to protect him. Sable's rage nearly breaks the alliance. Emotional beat: raw honesty; the worst truth offered freely.

chapters.title: The Cipher of Her Leaving
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Grieving and furious, Sable deciphers the journal alone using her own childhood memories as the key, discovering Yara went to the Understar deliberately—to seal it from inside. The stars going out means the seal is failing. Emotional beat: understanding replacing blame; resolve kindling.

chapters.title: Down Through the Wardbones
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The pair descends beneath Vell into the wardbones—the ancient structure the city's defenses were built upon—guided by the sigil's pull. They evade Inquisition sappers and find evidence others have walked this path recently. Emotional beat: wonder and claustrophobia; the city revealed as a shell over older magic.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Net
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Ambushed in the wardbones by Brannoc and his wardens, Kestrel bargains with stolen memories of the Captain's dead son—an act that shames them both. They escape when the sigil flares and collapses the tunnel behind them. Emotional beat: mercy as weapon; enemies humanized.

chapters.title: What Stealing Costs
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confronts Kestrel about the memories he takes—each one leaves a hollow in the giver. She makes him swear never to steal from her, then teaches him Yara's counter-art: giving memories back. Emotional beat: tenderness emerging from distrust; the theme crystallized.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. They reach a cavern where the Thorn Court's agents have hollowed out memory-stolen citizens into mindless servants singing the seal's failing song. Kestrel recognizes one voice as Odile's. Emotional beat: horror at magic weaponized; personal stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: Ashvine's Bargain, Revisited
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ashvine corners them again, revealing Yara is alive inside the Understar, sustained as its unwilling anchor. He offers safe passage—for the sigil. Sable, tempted by her mother, nearly accepts before Kestrel refuses for them both. Emotional beat: love versus principle; fracture and repair.

chapters.title: The Door That Eats Names
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the threshold of the Understar, the door demands a name as toll. Kestrel gives up his own—becoming nameless, unremembered even by the wards—and the way opens. Sable holds his hand so she won't forget him. Emotional beat: self-erasure as sacrifice; devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Understar
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Inside, they find Yara fused to the failing seal, half-dissolved into light, and learn the truth: the sigil was always meant to return here, carried by someone willing to stay. Ashvine arrives, wanting the seal broken and the old war reignited. Emotional beat: awe, reunion, and imminent ruin.

chapters.title: The War Beneath the Skin
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Battle within the Understar: Ashvine against Kestrel, Sable against the hollow choir, Yara fading. Kestrel realizes brute force fails—the seal mends only with freely given memory. He begins pouring in everything: Yara's face, Sable's laughter, his own name. Emotional beat: climactic sacrifice begun.

chapters.title: Everything I Kept
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. As Kestrel empties himself into the seal, Sable does the unthinkable: she steals memories back from the seal and returns them to him, piece by piece, keeping only enough to keep the stars lit. Yara, freed, spends her last strength binding Ashvine into the stone. Emotional beat: love answering sacrifice; the rule broken rightly.

chapters.title: Stars, Relit
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. They emerge changed: the stars burn again, the wards hold, and Kestrel remembers almost everything—but not all, and not why he sometimes weeps at candlelight. Brannoc lets them walk away, having seen what they gave. Emotional beat: exhausted grace; survival with scars.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's New Trade
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Months later, Kestrel and Sable run a quiet shop where Kestrel practices Yara's counter-art—returning stolen memories to those who sold them, one client at a time. Among returned memories, people begin remembering magic kindly. Emotional beat: healing as vocation; inheritance transformed.

chapters.title: Yara and the Sigil
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. On the anniversary of the stars' return, Kestrel finds a sealed letter in his own handwriting that he doesn't remember writing: Yara's final message, which he hid from himself. It tells him what he chose to forget—that she named the sigil after him, her second chance. Emotional beat: bittersweet closure; memory as legacy.
